attacks.claim: The go.mod `replace` points zap at a local path outside the repo. A clean-checkout CI build cannot resolve `../zap`, so the build breaks. Where a `../zap` does exist, the binary shipped to on-call laptops embeds unreviewed local source. The pinned pseudo-version is silently overridden, so the stated zap bump has no effect on the built code.

printPlan does not mirror computeBatches. It sizes batches from len(hosts) without ceil and without excluding the canary, and it iterates over all hosts, so the canary is printed twice. The printed plan will differ from what the real rollout executes, which defeats the feature's purpose of letting on-call trust the plan. Example: 10 hosts, canary set, MaxSurge 0.25. The real run gives 1 canary batch plus ceil(9*0.25)=3-host batches, which is 4 batches. The dry run prints int(10*0.25)=2-host batches over all 10 hosts, which is 6 batches with the canary repeated.
attacks.evidence: per := int(float64(len(hosts)) * o.MaxSurge) ... for i := 0; i < len(hosts); i += per  vs  size := int(math.Ceil(float64(len(rest)) * o.MaxSurge))
